History:
• 26-year-old male presents with 3 hours of sudden “tight” chest  
• Associated mild shortness of breath, wheeze, and non-productive cough  
• Recent viral URTI last week (sore throat, runny nose; now improved except for persistent cough)  
• Dyspnea worsens on exertion (e.g., climbing stairs); no dyspnea at rest  
• Denies chest pain; describes inability to “get a full breath in”  
• No sputum, fever, throat swelling, or ear pain

Past Medical History:
• Asthma (hospitalized with intubation at age ≈17)  
• Allergic rhinitis/hay fever; dust allergy  
• Childhood eczema; childhood milk-protein allergy  
• No known drug allergies  
• Family: Mother – eczema; Father – asthma

Medications:
• Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (ran out 1 week ago)  
• Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented (ran out 1 week ago)

Physical Examination:
• Video consult; patient alert, conversing in full sentences  
• No visible respiratory distress at rest  
• Reports wheeze and exertional shortness of breath  
• No chest wall tenderness reported  
• No objective vitals, peak flow, or auscultation available

Impression:
Acute mild-to-moderate asthma exacerbation likely precipitated by recent viral infection and interruption of controller/reliever inhalers.

Management Plan:
• Prescribed Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler for PRN relief  
• Prescribed Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler for regular controller therapy  
• Prescribed 5-day course of oral corticosteroid (exact drug/dose not documented; instructed “2 tablets in the morning”)  
• Issued prescription for a spacer device and provided usage instructions  
• Advised:  
  – Resume Clenil daily once symptoms improve  
  – Use Ventolin as needed; if ≥ 1 puff every 3 hours, seek medical review  
  – Monitor for steroid side effects (mood changes, hyperglycemia, rash, nausea, headache)  
  – Rest and consider time off work; may self-certify first 7 days  
  – Seek urgent care for worsening breathlessness, chest tightness/pain, light-headedness, or any concern

Patient Summary:
26-year-old asthmatic male with recent cold now experiencing 3 hours of chest tightness, wheeze, and mild SOB. Assessment consistent with asthma flare due to missed inhalers. Provided rescue/controller inhalers, short course oral steroids, spacer, and safety-net advice.

Key Takeaways:
• Start oral steroid course immediately: 2 tablets each morning for 5 days.  
• Use Ventolin via spacer PRN; if needed more often than every 3 hours, get medical help.  
• Restart Clenil inhaler daily once acute symptoms settle to prevent future attacks.

Next Steps:
• Obtain prescriptions within the hour; begin medications today.  
• Arrange follow-up with primary care/GP after completing steroid course or sooner if symptoms worsen.  
• Consider peak-flow meter for home monitoring at future visit.

• Missing expected elements: objective vitals, peak-flow reading, detailed respiratory exam, exact steroid name/dose, inhaler dosages, immunization status.  
• No internal transcript conflicts noted.
